pack.title: World History & Myth
pack.description: Ancient places, enduring stories, and words with a past.

categories.title: ROMAN DEITIES
categories.triviaFact: Vesta was associated with the hearth and the sacred fire of ancient Rome.

categories.title: GREEK LETTERS
categories.triviaFact: The English word alphabet combines the names of the first two Greek letters.

categories.title: HISTORIC WRITING SURFACES
categories.triviaFact: Papyrus sheets were made from strips cut from the stem of a wetland plant.

categories.title: BEFORE AGE
categories.triviaFact: The Bronze Age takes its name from an alloy commonly made with copper and tin.

redHerrings.note: MARS and NEPTUNE suggest planets, but JUNO and VESTA complete the Roman deities; this board has no four-planet set.

categories.title: GREEK MYTHIC HEROES
categories.triviaFact: The Odyssey follows Odysseus on his troubled journey home from Troy.

categories.title: ANCIENT MONUMENTS
categories.triviaFact: Stonehenge includes stones brought from places far from its Salisbury Plain setting.

categories.title: HISTORIC NAVIGATION TOOLS
categories.triviaFact: A sextant measures the angle between two visible objects, often a star and the horizon.

categories.title: BEFORE HORSE
categories.triviaFact: A clothes horse is a frame used to hold garments while they dry.

redHerrings.note: TROJAN recalls the war of ACHILLES and ODYSSEUS, but is not a hero's name; the four HORSE compounds resolve it.

categories.title: EGYPTIAN DEITIES
categories.triviaFact: Anubis was associated with embalming and was often depicted with a jackal-like head.

categories.title: ARCHITECTURAL FEATURES
categories.triviaFact: A keystone is the central wedge-shaped stone at the top of an arch.

categories.title: ANCIENT AMERICAN CULTURES
categories.triviaFact: The Inca used knotted cords called quipus to record information.

categories.title: ALSO VERBS FOR SUPPORTING
categories.triviaFact: To brace something is to strengthen it against pressure or movement.

redHerrings.note: PROP and BRACE sound like structural features, but join BACK and BEAR as verbs meaning to support.

categories.title: ROYAL TITLES
categories.triviaFact: Tsar developed from Caesar, showing how a personal name could become a title.

categories.title: NORSE MYTHIC FIGURES
categories.triviaFact: In Norse mythology, Thor carries a hammer called Mjolnir.

categories.title: ANCIENT TRADE GOODS
categories.triviaFact: Incense was traded for use in religious ceremonies and for its fragrance.

categories.title: FOLLOW CROWN
categories.triviaFact: Crown land refers to land held by the monarch or state under a country's legal system.

redHerrings.note: PRINCE seems to make a fifth royal title, but CROWN JEWELS, CROWN COURT and CROWN LAND make the intended phrase set.

categories.title: MYTHIC CREATURES
categories.triviaFact: A werewolf is a human who transforms into a wolf in European folklore.

categories.title: LANDMARKS IN ASIA
categories.triviaFact: Angkor Wat was originally built as a Hindu temple and later became a Buddhist site.

categories.title: WORDS FROM ARABIC
categories.triviaFact: Algebra derives from an Arabic term connected with restoring or completing.

categories.title: FOLLOW SILVER
categories.triviaFact: A silver lining uses the bright edge of a cloud as a metaphor for hope.

redHerrings.note: BULLET recalls silver bullets and WEREWOLF, but SILVER also makes established phrases with LINING, SCREEN and SPOON.

categories.title: HISTORIC WRITING SYSTEMS
categories.triviaFact: Linear B was used to write an early form of the Greek language.

categories.title: HISTORIC SEAFARING PEOPLES
categories.triviaFact: Polynesian navigators used stars, swells and other natural cues to cross the Pacific.

categories.title: MYTHIC UNDERWORLD FIGURES
categories.triviaFact: Charon ferries the dead across a river in Greek underworld mythology.

categories.title: BEFORE SHIP
categories.triviaFact: Friendship once used a suffix meaning a state or condition, also found in fellowship.

redHerrings.note: CHARON ferries passengers and so tempts a seafaring group, but his three partners also belong to underworld myths.

categories.title: GREEK PHILOSOPHERS
categories.triviaFact: Socrates left no known writings of his own, so his ideas survive through other authors.

categories.title: ROMAN PUBLIC STRUCTURES
categories.triviaFact: Roman basilicas served public and legal functions before the term became linked to churches.

categories.title: HISTORIC ART MATERIALS
categories.triviaFact: Lapis lazuli was ground to make the blue pigment traditionally called ultramarine.

categories.title: WORDS WITH SILENT INITIAL LETTERS
categories.triviaFact: The silent initial letter in knight reflects changes in English pronunciation.

redHerrings.note: KNIGHT and GNOME suggest medieval fantasy, but WRIST and PSALM reveal the shared silent initial letters.

categories.title: HISTORIC RULERS
categories.triviaFact: Augustus became the first Roman emperor after the end of the Roman Republic.

categories.title: WORDS FROM PERSONAL NAMES
categories.triviaFact: Braille takes its name from Louis Braille, who developed the tactile reading system.

categories.title: WORDS USING ONLY ROMAN NUMERAL LETTERS
categories.triviaFact: These words use only Roman numeral letters, though they need not form valid numbers.

categories.title: BEFORE MARK
categories.triviaFact: A hallmark originally identified an official assay of a precious metal.

redHerrings.note: CAESAR recalls a salad beside SANDWICH, but on this board CAESAR completes four rulers; the named inventions have their own set.
